### [Effective harnesses for long-running agents](<https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-harnesses-for-long-running-agents>)

This harness separates initial environment setup from repeated implementation sessions, using a feature list, progress records, version history, and end-to-end tests to preserve continuity. It gives builders a concrete pattern for making incremental progress across context resets and detecting premature completion.

**Published:** 2025-11-26 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:13:56.564Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** Long-Horizon, Reliability, Coding

**Evidence:** engineering-report; full-text. The November 26, 2025 article connects observed long-running coding failures to specific harness mechanisms and supplies an accessible autonomous-coding example. The source explains initialization, session recovery and browser-based verification.

**Limitations:** The demonstration targets full-stack web development and is not a broad controlled benchmark. Generalization to other domains and the best division of work between agents remain open; browser-tool limitations still leave verification gaps.

## [2026-09-29 — Landscape baseline](../../../landscape/2026-09-29.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Learning Meta-Skills for Agent Harness Design in Test-Time AI4AI](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38143>)

A builder agent extracts reusable support principles from development-task feedback and converts them into task-specific tools, context, memory, and execution controls for another agent. The method explores improving an agent's environment without changing either model's weights, turning prior failures into reusable harness-design knowledge.
